title: Onramp orchestration: automated weight ingestion, conversion verification, version pinning and profile publication
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Build an end-to-end orchestrator that automates the lifecycle from community weight upload to published model + performance profile in the catalog. The orchestrator must: (1) accept raw archive uploads and metadata (checksum, license, author), (2) run deterministic conversion in a containerized runner (conversion image pinned by digest), (3) validate byte-level checksum and execution smoke tests across fp16/int8 variants, (4) run the standard microbench and quality eval suite, (5) produce a content-addressable artifact and semantic version tag, (6) publish performance profile to the catalog and mark the model as 'candidate' or 'approved' based on gating rules. This ticket delivers the orchestration DAG, gating logic, and a minimal UI for manual override/inspection.
acceptance_criteria: Given a validated weight archive, the orchestrator completes conversion and validation pipeline without manual intervention in >90% of cases
All produced artifacts are content-addressable (sha256) and stored in S3 with metadata JSON matching catalog schema
Performance profile (latency/p50, p95; throughput; memory) and qual eval summary are published to the model catalog UI and are queryable by runtime
Gate tests enforce license check, checksum match, conversion smoke, and quality threshold; failures create reproducible debug bundles and a Slack alert to #model-onboard
steps: weights intake endpoint accepts .tar.gz and metadata.json; run basic sanitizers (filetypes, size, license)
stage archive to ephemeral bucket and calculate sha256; spawn conversion job using conversion-container:sha256
conversion job outputs model artifacts in runtime-friendly format (tokenizer, config, model.bin variants); run deterministic smoke run using reference prompt set
profile job executes microbench with three sequence lengths and two batch sizes across baseline kernels; capture p50/p95/alloc
eval job runs small sample of alignment/qa prompts and compares to baseline thresholds; compute quality delta
publish step writes model manifest (id, semantic_version, tags, checksums, profile) to catalog and triggers dashboard update
if any gating step fails, collect debug bundle (logs, conversion container image digest, failing examples) and create ENG ticket automatically for manual triage
notes: Decision: Use content-addressable artifact IDs + semantic version where semver is incremented only on deterministic weight changes (not metadata edits)
Trade-off: Running full eval suite increases onboarding latency — we will gate by default on a lightweight quality smoke and run full eval asynchronously; catalog will mark 'profiling in progress'
Risk: Some community weights use non-standard tokenizers; added tokenizer normalization shim as a best-effort step and flag for manual review
Operational: Conversion containers must be pinned by digest and kept in the internal registry; retention policy for ephemeral buckets = 30 days after onboarding
